newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE REACHES END OF LINE IN WALLABY WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMPESE REACHES END OF LINE IN WALLABY WIN.

text.p: David Campese ended his test career in muted fashion on Sunday as Australia recorded a 28-19 victory over Wales to complete a clean sweep of international victories on their European tour.
The world record try-scorer barely had a chance to add to his tally of 64 test tries on his 101st appearance but at least had the satisfaction of helping create one of the Wallabies' three tries.

It was Campese's superb spiralling punt to the corner which set up the lineout from which Michael Brial crashed over in the first half, although Australia's victory remained in doubt until they were awarded a penalty try in the final minute.

Wales trailed 18-6 at half time but their hopes were dramatically re-ignited 13 minutes into the second half when centre Gareth Thomas intercepted a pass from George Gregan and raced 90 metres to score under the Wallaby posts and bring his side within two points.
Jonathan Davies converted and then landed his fourth successful penalty to put Wales 19-18 ahead with 20 minutes left. But it was a lead which always looked vulnerable.
The Wallabies had squandered at least two previous try-scoring chances, but their pack kept play firmly camped in the Welsh 22 and were rewarded for their persistence.

Australian full-back Matthew Burke finished with a personal haul of 18 points, establishing a world record for the highest test aggregate scored by one player in a calendar year. He has scored 189 points in 11 games, eight more than Welshman Neil Jenkins managed in 12 matches in 1994.

The encounter had been billed as a mouthwatering clash between Campese and Davies, making his return to the Welsh union side after an eight-year gap, but kicking apart, both 34-year-olds spent long periods as virtual spectators.

The prospects of Davies's test career extending much longer than Campese's certainly looked doubtful at half time, Burke's 11th-minute try when he beat a startled Ieuan Evans to a loose ball having visibly sapped Welsh confidence.

Thomas's try was a much-needed stroke of luck and Davies did his best to fuel a revival, bravely retaining the kicking duties despite the presence of specialist Neil Jenkins on the field as a replacement.
In the end, though, Australia pulled away in similar fashion to their wins against Italy, Scotland and Ireland to record their sixth straight victory over Wales.
Coach Greg Smith is still rebuilding for the 1999 World Cup but will continue to search for a player capable of matching Campese's achievements.

Wales - 15-Wayne Proctor (16-Neil Jenkins, 50th); 14-Ieuan Evans, 13-Gareth Thomas, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Dafydd James; 10-Jonathan Davies, 9-Rob Howley; 8-Steve Williams, 7-Kingsley Jones, 6-Hemi Taylor (18-Colin Charvis, 16th), 5-Derwyn Jones (19-Craig Quinnell, 70th), 4-Gareth Llewellyn, 3-David Young, 2-Jonathan Humphreys, 1-Christian Loader.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Joe Roff, 13-Jason Little, 12-Tim Horan (captain), 11-David Campese; 10-Pat Howard, 9-George Gregan; 8-Michael Brial, 7-David Wilson, 6-Owen Finegan, 5-David Giffin, 4-Tim Gavin, 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Dan Crowley.
